note: git checkout -- . --quiet SILENTLY LEAVES THE TREE DIRTY. Putting --quiet AFTER the -- separator makes git read it as a pathspec, so the command exits 1 complaining the pathspec did not match any files, and a defensive 2>/dev/null || true swallows that. Proven in an isolated repo: with the flag after the separator, exit=1 and the file is still modified; with the flag before it, exit=0 and the tree is clean. Two second-order lessons worth more than the fix: (1) a line whose entire job is leaving a checkout clean can fail while reporting success, so check git status --porcelain instead of trusting exit=0 -- that is how this was found, in a scheduled job that runs unattended nightly; (2) the defensive || true that makes a script robust is exactly what hides the failure, so pair every || true with a positive check of the state it was meant to produce.
